title: Diagnostic accuracy of AI-augmented renal ultrasound for degenerative kidney disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Diagnostic accuracy of AI-augmented renal ultrasound for degenerative kidney disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p2】Despite these advancements, the literature on AI and radiomics in ultrasound for degenerative kidney disorders remains fragmented, with varying methodologies, sample sizes, and validation approaches across studies [4,5]. This systematic review aims to critically appraise and synthesize the existing evidence on the application of AI and radiomics in ultrasound imaging for the diagnosis, monitoring, and management of degenerative kidney disorders.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Degenerative kidney disorders encompass conditions such as chronic kidney disease (CKD) [1]. Ultrasound imaging has emerged as a cornerstone diagnostic tool in nephrology due to its noninvasive nature, real-time capabilities, cost-effectiveness, and lack of ionizing radiation, enabling the assessment of renal morphology, vascularity, and parenchymal changes [2]. However, conventional ultrasound interpretation relies heavily on subjective visual assessment by clinicians, which can be limited by inter-observer variability, challenges in quantifying subtle textural abnormalities, and difficulties in early detection of degenerative processes [3].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Diagnostic accuracy of AI-augmented renal ultrasound for degenerative kidney disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · S0002-p1】This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines [6]. The review protocol was prospectively registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) under registration number CRD420261277386. No amendments were made to the protocol during the review process. The methods adhered to established standards for systematic reviews in medical imaging and artificial intelligence applications, ensuring transparency, reproducibility, and minimization of bias.

【Data collection and items · S0002-S2004-p1】Data extraction was performed independently by two reviewers using a standardized, piloted form in Microsoft Excel. Extracted items included: study characteristics (author, year, country, design, sample size); population details (age, sex, disorder type, disease stage); intervention specifics (AI algorithm type, radiomics features used, ultrasound modality [e.g., B-mode, Doppler]); comparator details; outcomes (primary and secondary metrics with confidence intervals); validation methods (e.g., cross-validation, external cohorts); and funding sources/conflicts of interest. For radiomics studies, additional items included feature selection methods, software used, and adherence to the Radiomics Quality Score 2.0 (RQS 2.0). Discrepancies in data extraction were resolved by consensus [7]. Potential overlap between study populations was assessed by comparing study centers, recruitment periods, participant characteristics, sample sizes, ultrasound platforms, and author groups. When publications appeared to originate from potentially overlapping cohorts, they were treated as separate reports only when they evaluated distinct imaging approaches, outcomes, or independently defined datasets; possible residual cohort overlap was considered when interpreting the evidence.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Diagnostic accuracy of AI-augmented renal ultrasound for degenerative kidney disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Overview of the evidence base and principal findings · S0004-S2001-p1】This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized evidence from 31 studies evaluating artificial intelligence and radiomics applications in ultrasound for degenerative kidney disorders. The quantitative meta-analysis of 28 diagnostic studies revealed robust performance, with machine learning models achieving pooled sensitivity of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82–0.90) and specificity of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.79–0.87), while deep learning models demonstrated superior discrimination with sensitivity of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.84–0.93) and specificity of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.81–0.91). These findings suggest that AI-augmented ultrasound has promising diagnostic performance; however, the magnitude and generalizability of this benefit remain uncertain because of substantial clinical and statistical heterogeneity. Importantly, diagnostic detection, disease-severity classification, histopathological phenotyping, and longitudinal prognostic prediction represent distinct clinical questions; accordingly, these applications are interpreted separately throughout the narrative synthesis rather than regarded as interchangeable measures of AI performance. Across the included evidence, a consistent pattern emerged: models that quantify parenchymal microstructural and functional information (e.g., radiomics texture, viscoelasticity, microvascular flow) generally outperformed conventional B-mode assessment alone, particularly for tasks where morphological changes are subtle (early CKD; early fibrosis; early diabetic nephropathy). For example, a deep learning radiomics approach using routine grey-scale ultrasound improved CKD detection and early-stage discrimination compared with radiologists, with strong performance for CKD vs non-CKD classification (AUC 0.918) and notably higher AUCs than senior readers for early stages (e.g., G1 and G2) [20]. Similarly, radiomics-clinical nomograms for renal pathology phenotyping (e.g., diabetic kidney disease glomerular status) improved discrimination relative to clinical-only or radiomics-only models, supporting the view that ultrasound-derived quantitative features provide complementary information to standard clinical indices [21]. At the same time, the evidence base remains dominated by single-center cohorts and internal validation strategies, which constrains inference about real-world generalizability. This tension—promising discrimination within curated datasets versus uncertain transportability—recurs across disease types and outcome definitions. The pooled estimates should nevertheless be interpreted as broad summary measures rather than disease-specific diagnostic benchmarks. The included studies addressed clinically distinct targets, including CKD detection and staging, renal fibrosis/IFTA assessment, diabetic kidney disease, transplant-related abnormalities, and pediatric nephropathies. These conditions differ in pathophysiology, reference standards, disease prevalence, and ultrasound manifestations; consequently, a single pooled estimate cannot be assumed to represent identical diagnostic performance across all clinical settings. The quantitative findings should therefore be considered complementary to the disease- and task-specific narrative synthesis presented in this review.

【Performance by AI algorithm type · S0004-S2002-p2】Multimodal fusion approaches consistently outperformed single-modality models across included studies. Chen and Wu et al. demonstrated that integrating grayscale ultrasound radiomics (AUC: 0.79), color Doppler radiomics (AUC: 0.70), and shear wave elastography (AUC: 0.74) achieved a combined AUC of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.82–0.94) for renal fibrosis classification, with reclassification analysis showing NRI of 65.5% and IDI of 12.4% compared to baseline models [12]. Qin similarly reported that ultrasound-based radiomics models (AUC: 0.894–0.919) outperformed both conventional color Doppler ultrasound parameters (AUC: 0.686–0.784) and isolated deep learning approaches (AUC: 0.670–0.880) [14].

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Diagnostic accuracy of AI-augmented renal ultrasound for degenerative kidney disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. PRISMA flow diagram.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. (A) Traffic light visualization of risk of bias and applicability concerns using PROBAST for all 31 included studies. The left panel displays risk of bias across four domains: participants (D1), predictors (D2), outcome (D3), and analysis (D4), with overall risk of bias summarized in the rightmost column. The right panel presents applicability concerns across three domains (D1, D2, D3), with overall applicability concerns summarized in the rightmost column. Green circles with plus signs (+) indicate low risk of bias or applicability concerns; yellow circles with minus signs (−) indicate unclear risk; red circles with (X) symbols indicate high risk of bias or applicability concerns. (B) Summary Proportions of Risk of Bias and Applicability Concerns. Stacked bar charts showing proportional distribution of PROBAST assessments for 31 included studies. (A) Risk of bias across four domains and overall assessment. (B) Applicability concerns across three domains and overall assessment. Color coding: green = low risk/concerns, yellow = unclear, red = high, dark red = critical, blue = no information. Bars represent percentages from 0% to 100%.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. (A) Heatmap visualization of RQS 2.0 across 13 included studies. The heatmap displays the distribution of scores across nine Radiomics Readiness Levels for each study, with total scores (out of 56) provided in brackets before author names. Each row represents one of nine RRLs, ranging from RRL1 (Foundational exploration) to RRL9 (Clinical deployment). The maximum scores for each Radiomics Readiness Level (RRL) are displayed in parentheses directly in the figure, following each RRL name on the y-axis. Cell values indicate the scores achieved by each study for the respective RRL criteria, with color intensity representing score magnitude (darker shades indicating higher scores). (B) Radiomics Readiness Level (RRL) Compliance. The compliance percentage for each study was calculated based on its corresponding Radiomics Readiness Level (RRL). This was determined as the ratio of the study’s achieved cumulative points to the maximum possible cumulative points for that RRL, multiplied by 100.
